Web design Long Beach CA owners can rely on begins with one fact people from elsewhere keep forgetting: Long Beach is not a neighborhood of Los Angeles. It is a city of its own, with its own port, its own city hall and its own shopping streets. A site that says "serving the LA area" makes a Long Beach business sound like it could be anywhere.

Maurice Johnson builds sites that name the real place. He writes every page himself from Big Sandy, Texas, shows you a free demo first, and charges $497, $997 or $1,997, once.

Long Beach website design for a city built around a port

Long Beach counted 466,742 residents in the 2020 census. Its economy has been tied to the harbor from the start: the Long Beach Area Chamber of Commerce began as a Board of Trade whose focus was largely the port, and it took its current name when it was incorporated in 1918. Today the Port of Long Beach is reported as the second busiest port in the nation, and it moved a record 9.6 million container units (TEUs) in 2024.

All that cargo supports a long chain of smaller firms: trucking companies, warehouses, customs brokers, equipment repair shops, staffing agencies and the lunch spots that feed their crews. Most of them win work from other businesses, and a logistics coordinator checking out a vendor wants specifics, not slogans.

What a port-side firm's site should list

  • What you haul, store or service, in the words shippers use.
  • Equipment, capacity and the area you cover.
  • Hours, including nights or weekends if you work them.
  • A quote form that emails every request straight to you.

What a shop on a Long Beach street needs

  • The street and district in the first lines of the page.
  • Hours, parking and whether you take walk-ins.
  • Photos of what you actually sell or make.
  • A phone number at the top that dials on one tap.

The shopping streets people name when they search

Long Beach runs business improvement districts along several of its commercial streets, and the city passes the assessments it collects back to each district's association. Here are streets a customer is likely to type.

  • Retro Row, 4th StreetVintage and collectible shops along East 4th Street. A boutique here should say "Retro Row" and "4th Street" in plain text, not only in a logo.
  • Belmont Shore, 2nd StreetA walkable run of boutiques, restaurants and nightlife near the water. On a busy street like this, parking tips earn their place on the page.
  • Bixby KnollsA north Long Beach district with its own business association and a strip of specialty shops.
  • East Village Arts DistrictThe downtown blocks between Alamitos Avenue and Long Beach Boulevard, known for galleries, boutiques and bars.
  • Cambodia Town, Anaheim StreetIn 2007 the city council gave the name Cambodia Town to a 1.2-mile business corridor on Anaheim Street between Atlantic and Junipero Avenues. Visit Long Beach says the city has the largest concentration of Cambodians of any city outside Cambodia.

Web design Long Beach CA shoppers see on the local map

Google says local results depend mostly on relevance, distance and prominence. A diner searching "pho near me" from Belmont Shore and one searching from Bixby Knolls will see different shops, because distance changes the answer. You cannot move your shop, but you can make it plain what you sell and where you are, and that is what relevance is made of.

So the page names the street and the district, lists the dishes or services in words people search, and matches your Google Business Profile. Nobody honest promises a ranking; we promise a site that is clearly about your business in your part of town.

Picking a package for a Long Beach business

A single storefront on 2nd Street rarely needs more than Starter: five pages for $497, live in 7 to 14 days, with a contact form, Google Maps and hours. A plumber or a mobile detailer who works Long Beach, Lakewood, Signal Hill and the cities beyond fits Pro at $997, which adds a gallery, Google Business Profile setup and ten city pages each written for its own town; its AI chat widget is free for 14 days, then $297 a month. Hosting, maintenance and updates come to $49 a month, or are included while you keep the AI agent. We do not sell page counts. A page earns its place by answering a real customer's question.

Long Beach help that costs nothing

The Small Business Development Center hosted by Long Beach City College offers one-on-one advising at no charge, plus workshops on planning, finance and marketing. It belongs to the Los Angeles Regional SBDC network and is funded by the SBA and the state's GO-Biz office. The city's BizPort website, launched in 2016, gathers the steps for a city business license and points owners to other programs. And the Long Beach Area Chamber of Commerce, which grew out of that port-minded Board of Trade, is another way to meet the owners and buyers around you.

Common questions

How much do web designers charge for a website in Long Beach?

It depends on the designer and how much is custom, and a lot of firms in the Los Angeles area quote only after a meeting. Ours are printed: Starter $497, Pro $997, Agency $1,997, each a one-time price. Hosting, maintenance and updates cost $49 a month, or nothing extra while you keep the AI agent.

Should my Long Beach website say Los Angeles?

Lead with Long Beach. It is a separate city, and people who live there search for it by name. If you also take work in Lakewood, Signal Hill or parts of Los Angeles, give each of those places its own page that describes the work you do there. A page about Los Angeles in general helps nobody choose you.

Can you build a website for a trucking, warehouse or customs business near the port?

Yes. Those sites are less about photos and more about plain answers: what you move or store, the equipment and capacity you have, your hours, the area you cover and how to request a quote. A shipper's coordinator wants to find that in a minute. If you need a customer portal or shipment tracking tied to your own systems, that is custom software outside our packages, and we will say so up front.

Is this page about Long Beach, California or Long Island, New York?

Long Beach, California, the city on San Pedro Bay in Los Angeles County. There is also a city called Long Beach on Long Island, and web design searches for Long Island are a different market. This page is only about the California city.

My shop is in a business improvement district. Should the website mention it?

Mention the district by the name customers use, such as Belmont Shore or Bixby Knolls, because that is how they search. Link to the district's events page if it runs street fairs or seasonal promotions that bring people to your door.
